subject: ela
intro: On the SAT, 'Command of Evidence: Textual' questions ask which quotation or finding most directly supports (or sometimes weakens) a given claim. The right choice must connect specifically to the claim stated in the question, not just to the general topic.

items.prompt:
Claim: 'The new teaching method improved student writing.'

Which finding would BEST support this claim?
(A) Students said the class was fun.
(B) After the method, students' essay scores rose by 18%.
(C) The teacher had 10 years of experience.

steps: I need evidence that writing improved.
Essay scores rising directly measures improved writing.
solution.answer: (B) After the method, students' essay scores rose by 18%.

items.prompt: Why is 'students said the class was fun' NOT the best support for that claim?

steps: Enjoyment is not the same as improved writing.
So it does not directly support the specific claim.
solution.answer: Enjoyment does not directly measure improved writing.

items.prompt: To support a specific claim, evidence must connect to the ____, not just the topic.
Evidence must directly support the ____ in the question.
Evidence loosely about the topic but not the claim is ____.
Some questions ask which finding ____ a claim.
